scope: Read-only diagnosis of the first Guard service failure; no new inference performed for this diagnosis.

confirmed.five_transport_error_records_followed: 366 through 370; failures are not SAFE verdicts

diagnosis.confirmed_failure_class: System commit exhaustion coinciding with the Guard process allocation failure.
diagnosis.not_established: The exact allocator or library responsible for accumulated memory is not established. The tokenizers.pyd fault identifies the failing allocation site, not necessarily the source of earlier memory growth.
source_findings: Original server creates a new HTTP handler thread for each request and serializes model execution with a lock.
Inference uses torch.inference_mode(), use_cache=False, and local per-request tensors; no explicit retained list of per-request outputs is present.
The persistent label_vectors dictionary is not populated for the safety-only requests with an empty options list.
diagnosis.hypothesis: Fresh request threads may retain native/OpenMP/allocator resources, or dynamic-shape backend caches may accumulate. This requires memory observations and is not a proven tokenizer or PyTorch leak.

additive_mitigation.change: Substitute HTTPServer for serve.ThreadingHTTPServer; run the original serve.main().
additive_mitigation.health_check_caveat: Single-threaded HTTP serving cannot respond to health checks concurrently with inference.
additive_mitigation.validation_so_far: Wrapper syntax parsed only. Prediction parity and memory behavior must be checked by the active replay.
additive_mitigation.fallback: If memory continues growing, restart only the Guard service between bounded batches while retaining identical model settings and resuming only unscored inputs.
